lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Good morning Tamika! Thanks for picking up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, go ahead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How have you been feeling since we last talked?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I've had more energy, I noticed that.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That's great to hear.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Did you hit your goal this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Good! I didn't miss a day.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You kept going even on a hard week. That says a lot about you.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What's worked for you before?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I know I can do it, I did it before. My neighbor started doing it with me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Where could the walks after dinner fit in your day?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can probably manage three days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You kept going even on a hard week. That says a lot about you.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I mean, I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is that something you can do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I think so. If I plan it the night before, I can do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What did you notice on the days it went well?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Good question.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is your daughter able to help?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not yet. I put a reminder on the fridge.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've already started.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I guess.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That took effort.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I feel better about myself when I stick to it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why is this important to you right now?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Uh, being around for my family is why I'm doing this.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What could you try instead?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can stop eating at 8, I just need tea at night.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Black coffee, tea or water are fine during the fast. They don't break it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Walking hurts my knees, so why bother.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How do you want to handle the walks after dinner going forward?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay, this week I'll really do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've made up your mind.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Got it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need this for my head too, not just my body.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Finishing dinner a little earlier, like by 7, makes the 13 hours a lot easier.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Next week I want you to finish eating by 7:30 on 3 nights.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I guess.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If being so tired gets in the way again, what's your backup plan?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I'll ask my son to come with me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Let me make sure I got it. This week you did it 4 out of 4 days, the hard part was being so tired, and next week you're going to finish eating by 7:30 on 3 nights. Did I miss anything?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That's it exactly.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Monday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Talk soon!

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thank you, Pierre. Bye!

flags.reason: Gives unrequested advice to eat by 7 right after participant's change talk and ambivalence; no permission asked.
Directive new target (finish by 7:30 on 3 nights) pushed on a participant who answered 'I guess'; should be collaborative.
Knee pain as a barrier ('so why bother') was not explored; coach moved on without reflecting or problem-solving.
Verbatim repeat of line 8 out of context; signals scripted rather than attentive listening.

score.summary: The coach built good momentum with open questions and affirmations of Tamika's effort, and she voiced strong change talk about family and planning her walks. However, the coach directed a new eating-time goal after her ambivalence, repeated a canned affirmation, and did not explore her knee-pain barrier.
strengths: Open questions on lines 9, 17, 25 and 41 drew out change talk and her own backup plan.
Affirmations on lines 8, 21 and 23 recognized real effort and built confidence.
Clear summary and next-contact setting on lines 43 and 45 confirmed the plan with her.
coaching_tips: Line 37 and 39: offer options and ask permission before setting a new target, e.g., 'Would it help to look at your eating window together?'
Line 30: reflect the knee concern and explore it ('Walking is hard on your knees, so what would make it doable?') before moving on.
Line 13: avoid repeating earlier affirmations verbatim; reflect what the participant just said instead.
Line 34: check rather than assume the decision ('It sounds like you're leaning toward this week; how sure are you?').
